avoid_supplements.name: Vitamin D supplements (high-dose >4000 IU daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Excessive vitamin D increases serum calcium and may counteract calcitonin's hypocalcemic effects; increases risk of hypercalcemia
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin D supplementation to ≤2000 IU daily without physician approval; monitor serum calcium levels

avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements (>1200 mg elemental daily during therapy)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Excessive calcium supplementation may attenuate calcitonin-induced reduction in serum calcium and bone resorption benefits
avoid_supplements.action: Coordinate calcium intake with prescriber; ensure total dietary + supplemental calcium does not exceed RDA (1000-1200 mg daily)

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: High-dose magnesium may modulate calcium homeostasis; potential additive effects on mineral metabolism
caution_supplements.action: Monitor total magnesium intake; standard supplementation (200-400 mg daily) generally safe

caution_supplements.name: Phosphorus supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Phosphorus influences calcium-phosphate balance; excessive supplementation may affect calcitonin efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Avoid supplementation unless specifically directed; obtain phosphate levels via diet

avoid_foods.name: Fortified dairy products (milk, yogurt with high calcium content)
avoid_foods.mechanism: High dietary calcium may reduce calcitonin efficacy in lowering serum calcium; excessive intake impairs therapeutic response
avoid_foods.action: Moderate dairy intake to achieve RDA; coordinate total daily calcium with prescriber

avoid_foods.name: High-dose vitamin D-fortified foods (fortified cereals, supplements stacked with food)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Cumulative vitamin D from fortified foods + supplements increases hypercalcemia risk and reduces calcitonin efficacy
avoid_foods.action: Review all fortified food labels; limit cumulative vitamin D from all sources to <2000 IU daily

caution_foods.name: Leafy greens (spinach, kale) with high oxalate content
caution_foods.mechanism: Oxalates may marginally reduce calcium bioavailability; minimal clinical impact during calcitonin therapy
caution_foods.action: No restriction necessary; consumption supports overall bone health through other minerals

caution_foods.name: Salty foods and high sodium diet
caution_foods.mechanism: High sodium increases renal calcium excretion, which may complement calcitonin effects but causes unpredictable fluctuations
caution_foods.action: Maintain moderate sodium intake (<2300 mg daily) for cardiovascular and bone health

monitoring_notes: Calcitonin undergoes no hepatic CYP metabolism, minimizing direct drug interactions; monitor serum calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase periodically during therapy. Coordinate all calcium and vitamin D supplementation with the prescriber to prevent antagonism of calcitonin's therapeutic hypocalcemic and anti-resorptive effects.
